plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A hardy perennial prized for its dense, layered blooms in a wide range of forms, from pompons to spiders. It thrives in the cool, short days of autumn and is a mainstay of fall gardens and floral displays across the Northern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; native to East Asia (China and Japan)
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums have been cultivated in China for over 2,500 years, and in Japan the flower is the emblem of the Imperial family and the national flower.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, graceful tree with fern-like foliage that erupts into massive clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere spring, entire streets are carpeted in fallen purple blossoms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring (October to November in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia (Sydney, Brisbane), and Argentina
plants.funFact: Pretoria in South Africa is nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City' because of its roughly 70,000 jacaranda trees, which turn the city purple every October.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up delicate, crocus-like flowers in autumn without any leaves present. The foliage appears the following spring and dies back by summer, giving the plant its 'naked ladies' nickname.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (September to November)
plants.location: Damp meadows and woodlands of Europe, from the British Isles to central Europe
plants.funFact: Despite its name it is not a true crocus, and all parts are highly toxic because they contain colchicine, a compound used in medicine to treat gout.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: An airy annual with daisy-like flowers on slender stems above feathery foliage. In mild climates such as the southern United States and Mexico, it continues blooming into late autumn until the first hard frost.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer to late autumn; peak in warm regions through October and November
plants.location: Native to Mexico and Central America; naturalized across the Americas and in gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The name Cosmos comes from the Greek word for 'harmony' or 'ordered universe,' reflecting the symmetrical arrangement of its petals.
